name: Maitreya (the Christ / the World Teacher)
dom: world teaching; the love-wisdom principle; the office of the Christ; spiritual education of humanity
note: In Bailey's Theosophy, Maitreya is the Christ and World Teacher who heads the teaching department of the Spiritual Hierarchy under Sanat Kumara; fuses the Buddhist future-buddha Maitreya with the Theosophical office of 'the Christ.'

name: The Seven Rays
dom: seven streams of divine energy; will, love-wisdom, active intelligence, harmony, science, devotion, ceremonial order
note: The seven differentiated streams of divine energy (the Ray Lords and their qualities) that condition all souls and along which the Masters serve; modeled as one collective rather than seven entities.

name: The Solar Angel (Angel of the Presence)
dom: the higher self / soul; mediation between Monad and personality; egoic consciousness
note: In Bailey's esoteric psychology the soul/higher-self mediator overshadowing the human personality, called the 'Angel of the Presence'; an adaptation of older soul-guardian concepts.

name: Shamballa (the City of God)
dom: spiritual planetary centre; seat of the planetary Logos; the will-to-good
note: The highest of the three planetary spiritual centres in Bailey's cosmology, the 'City of God' where Sanat Kumara dwells; an adaptation of the Tibetan mythic kingdom of Shambhala.

name: The Manu
dom: will and government department of the Hierarchy; racial and political evolution; first-ray administration
note: The Master heading the will/government (first-ray) department of the Spiritual Hierarchy, paralleling the Christ (teaching) and the Maha Chohan (civilization); an adaptation of the Hindu Manu.

name: The Buddhas of Activity
dom: assistance to Sanat Kumara; transmission of cosmic energies; planetary administration at Shamballa
note: A collective of three exalted beings who assist Sanat Kumara at Shamballa, mediating cosmic energies to the planet; a Bailey-era elaboration of the Shamballa hierarchy.

name: The Master Jesus
dom: sixth ray of devotion and idealism; guidance of Christianity and the churches; discipleship
note: In Bailey's Theosophy a sixth-ray Master distinct from the Christ (Maitreya): the disciple-vehicle whose body 'the Christ' overshadowed, who now oversees the Christian churches; explicitly separate from the canonical Jesus Christ.

name: The Master Saint Germain (Rakoczi)
dom: seventh ray of ceremonial order and magic; civilization and culture; ritual and organization
note: The seventh-ray Chohan of ceremonial order and magic (the Master R. / Rakoczi); an adaptation built on the historical 18th-century Count of St Germain, recast as an ascended Master.

name: The Master Hilarion
dom: fifth ray of concrete knowledge and science; revelation of truth; the new science
note: The fifth-ray Chohan of concrete knowledge and science in Bailey's Theosophy; the name adapted from the early Christian ascetic St Hilarion.

name: The Master Serapis Bey
dom: fourth ray of harmony through conflict; beauty and the arts; aspiration and discipline
note: The fourth-ray Chohan of harmony-through-conflict in Bailey's system; a Master distinct from the Greco-Egyptian deity Serapis, the name being borrowed from it.

name: Ahriman
dom: materialism; mechanization; coldness; intellectual hardening; spiritual deadening
note: In Steiner's cosmology the cold, contracting adversary-being who drags humanity into materialism and denial of the spirit; the name is adapted from Zoroastrian Ahriman (Angra Mainyu) but the being is a distinct Anthroposophical re-conception.

name: Lucifer (Anthroposophical)
dom: pride; egotism; false spirituality; fantasy; inflation; illusion
note: Steiner's warm, expanding adversary-being of pride, fantasy, and false/inflated spirituality, the polar opposite of Ahriman; a deliberate re-conception that shares only the name with the Christian fallen-angel Lucifer.

name: The Asuras
dom: spirit-self corruption; egoity; destruction of the I; the most dangerous temptation
note: In Steiner's teaching the third and most dangerous class of adversary-beings, attacking the human spirit-self (the 'I'); the name is borrowed from the Indian asuras but designates a distinct Anthroposophical class.

name: Sorat
dom: anti-Christ force; the Sun-Demon; the Beast; the number 666; opposition to the Sun-Being
note: Steiner's Sun-Demon and Beast/Antichrist being, adversary of the Sun-Christ and associated with the number 666; named from the Agrippan solar spirit Sorath, distinct from the Lucifer-Ahriman-Asuras polarity.

name: The Representative of Humanity
dom: the Christ; the Sun-Being; balance; equilibrium between Lucifer and Ahriman; archetypal humanity
note: Steiner's figure of the Christ / Sun-Being who holds the central balance between the upward pull of Lucifer and the downward pull of Ahriman; an Anthroposophical interpretation of the Christ identified with Jesus Christ.

name: The Threefold Adversaries
dom: adversary powers; threefold opposition; the Lucifer-Ahriman-Asuras grouping
note: Collective grouping the three classes of adversary-being in Steiner's cosmology (Lucifer, Ahriman, and the Asuras), whose opposed pulls human spiritual development must learn to balance.

name: The Summerland
dom: afterlife; the spirit world; rest; progress of the soul; the pleasant abode of the dead
note: The Spiritualist afterlife or spirit world, conceived as a pleasant realm of rest and ongoing moral and spiritual progress; details vary widely across 19th-century Spiritualist sources.

name: Spirit Guides
dom: discarnate guidance; mediumship; communication with the living; spiritual instruction
note: The class of discarnate guiding spirits believed to communicate through and assist mediums; a practice-defined category rather than a fixed roster of named beings.

name: The Doorkeeper
dom: protection; gatekeeping; control of spirit access; guardianship of the medium
note: A protective guardian spirit in Spiritualist practice who controls which spirits are permitted to approach or communicate through a medium; a role-type whose identity varies by medium.
